goal: Test whether a scanned spectral peak is surprising relative to an estimated AR1 correlated-noise null, instead of treating peak height alone as an oscillation cause.

frozen_algorithm.baseline: SG040 predecision risk gate, detector and candidate challenge; threshold 0.45 comparator unchanged
frozen_algorithm.residuals: Linearly detrend last min(observed_n,160) samples, require >=100 observations
frozen_algorithm.null: Fit zero-intercept lag-one AR coefficient on detrended residuals, clipped to [-0.97,0.97]; estimate innovation sigma from detrended residual variance*(1-rho²); simulate stationary Gaussian AR(1) surrogates of equal length
frozen_algorithm.test_statistic: Maximum normalized Fourier power over periods 25,30,...,100 (16 frequencies); on each surrogate repeat detrending and max over same 16 periods
frozen_algorithm.allow_primary_on_disagreement: p<=0.0625; otherwise continue gathering data or unresolved at alarmed full decision
frozen_algorithm.no_future_samples: On every candidate time n, null fitted to observed continuation prefix only; no holdout truth label or future samples used.

pilot.note: Pilot used only for feasibility, runtime and inspection. Threshold fixed at discrete surrogate-tail resolution; not an independent holdout.

limitations: 31 surrogate draws produce coarse empirical p-values; p<=.0625 is not a formal familywise guarantee across sequential time inspections
AR1 Gaussian null is estimated on the same data and misspecified for changed correlation/non-Gaussian cases
Same observations and spectral search may share failures; not independent evidence ancestry
Synthetic data family and frequency range known in advance
Selective testing and repeated looks inflate eventual false-diagnosis risk absent further correction
